newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russian regional utilities support Moscow shares.
newsitem.headline: Russian regional utilities support Moscow shares.

text.p: Sharp growth in regional utilities traded in small volumes supported the Russian shares market on Tuesday, as investors continued to move from leading shares to less liquid, less well known ones, dealers said.
"There is a continuing demand for regional companies which are holding up the blue chips," said Peter Kizenko of ING Bank.
The Russian Trading System index was flat at 190.88 after 190.65 on Monday on $19.7 million trading volume in the market.
Chelyabenergo, a Ural area utility which did not trade on Monday, rose to $0.180 in late trading on 750,000 shares volume from a previous trade of $0.112 on November 4.
Samarenergo rose to $0.40 from $0.35 and Krasnoyarskenergo, in Siberia, rose to $0.34 from $0.23 on November 13, the previous trading date.

Traders said the trend towards less well known companies was strong, though they said that established firms with American Depositary Receipt programmes offering foreign investors Russian stocks on non-Russian markets could still show growth.
Andrei Galperin of Credianstalt-Grant did not see investors in leading shares taking profits by the end of the year.
Hedge funds and other investors hunting undervalued shares can force up prices sharply in illiquid, less traded shares.
Mosenergo, one of the leading and most liquid stocks, was not among the top 10 shares traded by volume although it saw close to $450,000 trade, closing at $0.989 after $0.988 on Monday.
